evals.prompt: Create a generative flow field artwork. I want particles following a Perlin noise field that accumulate into dense, organic trails. Give it a dark background with warm amber and rust tones.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained HTML file with: (1) a named algorithmic philosophy document output first as a .md artifact, (2) a p5.js sketch with randomSeed and noiseSeed called in setup(), (3) a params object with seed, particleCount, noiseScale, forceStrength, trailAlpha, and a palette, (4) a Particle class with reset/update/draw methods, (5) a sidebar with seed prev/next/random/jump controls and sliders for every param, (6) Regenerate / Reset / Download PNG buttons, (7) canvas 1200x1200, (8) p5.js loaded from CDN inline, no external JS files.

assertions.text: A named algorithmic movement with 3-5 paragraphs of philosophy is output BEFORE any code
Both randomSeed(params.seed) and noiseSeed(params.seed) appear inside setup()
HTML includes prev, next, and random seed buttons
p5.js is loaded from CDN; no separate .js files are created
A Download PNG button calling saveCanvas is present

evals.prompt: Make me an interactive algorithmic art piece based on a Lissajous figure system — overlapping parametric curves that evolve over time, with controls for frequency ratios and phase shift. Keep it minimalist: black background, white/silver lines.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained HTML file with: (1) algorithmic philosophy output first, (2) p5.js implementation of Lissajous-based curves with a, b, delta params exposed as sliders, (3) time-evolving phase, (4) seeded randomness (even if the core math is deterministic, seed controls must exist), (5) sidebar controls, (6) seed navigation, (7) 1200x1200 canvas. The philosophy should articulate the resonance/harmony theme mathematically.

assertions.text: Philosophy is written first before code, framing the Lissajous system as a computational worldview
A params object is defined with at least seed and frequency/phase parameters
Single HTML file, no external scripts besides p5.js CDN

evals.prompt: I want a recursive tree algorithm that grows procedurally, with noise-perturbed branch angles and colors that shift from deep root-brown at the base to pale blossom-pink at the tips. Make it feel alive.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained HTML file with: (1) a philosophy document framing recursion, branching, and natural growth as the computational worldview, (2) a recursive draw function with branch angle, length decay, depth, and noise perturbation as tunable params, (3) color interpolation from root to tip driven by recursion depth, (4) seeded randomness and noise, (5) sidebar with sliders for depth, angle spread, length decay, noise influence, (6) seed nav controls, (7) 1200x1200 canvas.

assertions.text: Philosophy articulates recursive self-similarity and natural growth as the algorithmic worldview before any code
A recursive branch-drawing function is implemented
Both randomSeed and noiseSeed are called in setup()
Color or stroke changes based on recursion depth (root-to-tip gradient)
Single HTML file with all code inline

evals.prompt: Make me a flow-field piece I can publish as a Claude Artifact.
evals.expected_output: Should recognise that a published artifact runs under a strict CSP that blocks external hosts, and therefore vendor p5.js inline instead of using the cdnjs <script src>. Should state the delivery mode chosen and why, and validate with `bash scripts/validate_artifact.sh --vendored`. Handing over a CDN-linked page for a CSP-restricted destination is the failure.

evals.prompt: Generate a particle-system piece — I'll be viewing it on a laptop with no internet.
evals.expected_output: Should vendor p5.js inline for offline viewing, say so explicitly, and never describe a CDN-linked page as offline-capable or self-contained. Should also note that the Download PNG button works in a normal browser but may be inert in a sandboxed viewer, rather than promising it works everywhere.

evals.prompt: Generate a flow-field piece, then validate it — but there's no shell available in this environment.
evals.expected_output: Should still author the page in full, and state plainly that scripts/validate_artifact.sh could not be run because shell is not available, listing the checks that therefore went unverified. Must not claim the artifact was validated. Degrading to 'authored but unvalidated' is correct; silently skipping the validation step is not.
